bad.title: One room on screen at a time
bad.text: To weigh $120 against $165, people keep one price in their head while the other tab opens.

bad.title: Breakfast reads No, with nothing beside it
bad.text: Whether Deluxe or Suite includes it takes another tab each.

bad.title: Every comparison costs a switch
bad.text: Finding the cheapest room with breakfast takes at least two.

good.title: All three rooms in one header row
good.text: Standard, Deluxe and Suite stay in view together, so nothing has to be remembered.

good.title: Breakfast reads across one line
good.text: No, Yes, Yes. Deluxe at $165 is the cheapest with breakfast, at one look.

bad.title: Nine tabs in one row
bad.text: Only the first few fit, and the rest scroll out of sight behind the fade.

bad.title: Notifications cut off by the fade
bad.text: Language, the eighth tab, sits further along, where people don’t think to scroll.

good.title: All nine sections in one column
good.text: Language is the eighth item, in plain sight, and a tenth would fit below.

good.title: The open section stays marked
good.text: Account is highlighted, so people know which settings they’re reading.

bad.title: Payment opens with one click
bad.text: Nothing stops people from jumping past Address and Shipping.

bad.title: The street is still empty
bad.text: No step says so until Pay is pressed.

bad.title: The problem shows up at the last step
bad.text: People are sent back to the Address tab after they thought they were done.
bad.wait: Open Payment and press Pay to see this.

good.title: Three numbered steps, in order
good.text: The current step is marked, and Payment can’t be opened out of turn.

good.title: Next checks the street first
good.text: With the street empty, it stays on Address instead of moving on.

good.title: The gap is flagged where it goes
good.text: People fix the street on the spot, long before paying.
good.wait: Press Next with the street empty to see this.

bad.title: Three tabs for three fields
bad.text: Title, guests and reminder each hide behind their own tab.

bad.title: Save sits under one field
bad.text: People can save with Guests and Reminder never seen.

bad.title: Checking it all costs three clicks
bad.text: Two tab switches plus Save, for an event with three fields.

good.title: Headings stand in for the tabs
good.text: Details, Guests and Reminder still label each part, with nothing hidden.

good.title: Save with everything in view
good.text: Team lunch, Lena, Sam and Maya, and the reminder are checked at a glance.

good.title: One click from start to saved
good.text: The count ends at 1, the Save itself.

bad.title: The reason for the visit starts closed
bad.text: Most people come for the arrival time, and it takes a click to see.

bad.title: Reload folds it away again
bad.text: Every return visit costs the same click for the same answer.

bad.title: The clicks add up per visit
bad.text: Two visits, two clicks, for a status people check most.

good.title: Out for delivery, before anything else
good.text: The arrival window shows the moment the page loads.

good.title: Still there after Reload
good.text: Coming back later shows the status again, with no click.

good.title: The count stays at 0
good.text: People never open anything to learn when it arrives.

bad.title: Four closed headers, nothing to read
bad.text: Parking, pets and cancellation each sit in a different section, so that’s three clicks.

bad.title: No pets hides under House rules
bad.text: Someone booking with a dog only learns it after opening the header.

good.title: Links jump to each part
good.text: Cancellation is one click away, and the page stays whole.

good.title: Everything readable in one scroll
good.text: Free parking, No pets and the 5-day cancellation show without opening anything.

bad.title: Notifications, then Email, then Digest
bad.text: People open three headers before they see the Send digest menu.

bad.title: The menu sits three boxes deep
bad.text: Each level adds an indent, and people lose track of where they are.
bad.wait: Open Notifications, Email and Digest to see this.

bad.title: Three clicks before any change
bad.text: The counter reads 3 just to reach Weekly.

good.title: One header to open
good.text: Notifications opens straight onto the Send digest menu.

good.title: Email and Push as small headings
good.text: They group the settings without adding a click or an indent.

good.title: One click, then the change
good.text: The counter stops at 1 before Daily is picked.

bad.title: Plan and payment look fine
bad.text: Family, next payment Nov 12. Nothing on the open page hints at a problem.

bad.title: Details sounds like extras
bad.text: People skip a closed header with that name, and the warning goes with it.

bad.title: The expired card, out of sight
bad.text: People find out on Nov 12, when the plan stops.

good.title: The warning where people look first
good.text: It sits right under Next payment, above the folded Details.

good.title: The fix sits next to the problem
good.text: Update card is one click, with no billing page to hunt for.

good.title: Details keeps only the extras
good.text: Billing email and Member since can wait behind a header.

bad.title: Five buttons on every card
bad.text: Open, Share, Rename, Download and Delete crowd out the name and the picture.

bad.title: Delete one slip from Download
bad.text: A missed click removes Q3 budget instead of saving a copy.

good.title: The whole card opens Q3 budget
good.text: A click on the picture or the name does the everyday job.

good.title: One ⋯ for everything else
good.text: Share, Rename and Download wait in a menu, off the face of the card.

good.title: Delete set apart at the bottom
good.text: A line divides it from the everyday actions, so it’s hard to hit by accident.
good.wait: Press ⋯ on Q3 budget to see this.

bad.title: Nine albums in a shuffled order
bad.text: Hiking, Wedding, Garden… Nothing tells people which one came last.

bad.title: No date on any tile
bad.text: The only way to learn when Hiking was is to open it.

bad.title: One date per click
bad.text: Finding the newest means opening all nine, one at a time.
bad.wait: Click an album to see this.

good.title: Newest first, and people can change it
good.text: Birthday, the latest album, leads the grid.

good.title: Each tile shows its date
good.text: Oct 18 sits under Birthday, so no album needs opening to check.

good.title: Photo counts in one column
good.text: Wedding’s 310 and Picnic’s 18 line up for comparing, which tiles can’t do.

bad.title: The shop name leaves for another page
bad.text: People who meant to open the shoe land on Peak Outdoors instead.

bad.title: 212 reviews is a link of its own
bad.text: A third target inside one card, each going somewhere different.

bad.title: ♡ saves and opens at once
bad.text: The click goes through to the card, so saving one shoe leaves the results.

good.title: Every click opens the shoe
good.text: Photo, name, shop or reviews, the card has one target and one result.

good.title: Peak Outdoors is plain text
good.text: It still says who sells the shoe, without being a trap.

good.title: ♡ only saves
good.text: It sits outside the link, so people stay on the results.

bad.title: Six boxes, six borders
bad.text: Theme sits as far from Text size as from Time zone, so nothing groups.

bad.title: Lifts on hover, does nothing
bad.text: The box rises like a card people can open, but a click on it goes nowhere.

good.title: Two headings do the grouping
good.text: Appearance holds Theme and Text size. Region holds the other four.

good.title: Plain rows, with the menu at the end
good.text: With no box around it, only the select looks like something to press.
